components.gap: Source manuscript pp. 9-10 (held PDF pp. 10-11), inside this entry's own locators 'after def. 2.2, manuscript p. 10' (body l. 41) and 'manuscript p. 10' (l. 48) and the chapter's 'sec. 2, manuscript pp. 9-11' (l. 9), contains items on the input and its theory that are not supplied. (1) Scope and grounds of the robustness remark on H\cap M=\varnothing and H\cup M=V: the source says neither restriction would harm its study of computational issues because its results remain valid under both, that H\cap M=\varnothing holds in all but a few of its proofs, that H\cup M=V is assumed with rare exceptions, and that the remaining proofs are easily adapted; lines 40-41 reduce this to 'their results hold under either restriction', without saying these are the complexity results or giving the grounds. (2) The comparison attached to the positive-atom convention, 'cf. Konolige's causal theories [40] for a similar model', is omitted. (3) After 'We do not require T to be in any special form' the source adds that implementations usually put T in a special format, most commonly clausal form, and that clausal form does not affect the computational complexity of logic-based abduction; lines 50-52 keep only that T is unrestricted. (4) The theory forms the source defines on p. 9 and uses to single out restricted variants of T are not supplied or related to the unrestricted T of def:p16-abduction-input: clauses as disjunctions of pairwise distinct literals identified with their literal sets, Horn (k<=1) and definite Horn (k=1) clauses, clausal-form theories, CNF and DNF. (5) Lesser p. 9 notation, also absent: a theory also denotes the conjunction of its formulas, and E_{\phi(X)}, the formula obtained by replacing each variable x of X by \top or \bot according to \phi(x).

components.gap: Source manuscript pp. 10-11 (held PDF pp. 11-12), the span this entry cites ('def. 2.3 and following discussion', body l. 187) together with the chapter's 'sec. 2, manuscript pp. 9-11' (l. 9), is narrowed to the two unpacked families. (1) The general formulation is absent: preference relations are modelled as preorders \preceq on 2^H because reflexivity and transitivity are the natural axioms; a\prec b means a\preceq b and not b\preceq a; Def. 2.3 defines Sol_\preceq(P) as the \prec-minimal solutions; and Sol(P)=Sol_=(P). (2) Lines 185-187 assert that MinExpl and CardExpl are the source's criteria without the written computation that the strict part of \subseteq is proper inclusion and the strict part of the size order \le is |S'|<|S|, so the identification rests on the citation. (3) Def. 2.4 (\preceq is irredundant iff S\subset S' implies S\prec S' for solutions S, S'), its attribution to [59, 69, 6, 40], the statements that \subseteq and \le are irredundant orders and that the subset-minimality order 'is just irredundancy itself', and the source's name 'irredundant solutions' for Sol_\subseteq(P) are omitted. (4) Lemma 2.2 (p. 11) is neither stated nor proved: for PAPs P_1,...,P_n with pairwise disjoint variable sets and the componentwise union problem, Sol_\preceq of the union equals {S_1\cup...\cup S_n : S_i\in Sol_\preceq(P_i)} when \preceq is equality, \subseteq or \le; it concerns exactly Expl, MinExpl and CardExpl, and the source gives no proof, so written steps are owed. (5) 'The main problems' and Def. 2.5 (p. 11) are absent: existence of a solution, \preceq-relevance (h lies in some \preceq-preferred solution) and \preceq-necessity (h lies in all of them), the division of H into not relevant, relevant but not necessary, and necessary hypotheses (true as a partition only when Sol_\preceq(P) is nonempty: with no solution every hypothesis is vacuously necessary and also not relevant), the terms \preceq-irrelevant and \preceq-dispensable (necessity is called indispensability in [36]), dropping the prefix for equality, and the remark that necessity results are corollaries of dispensability results. Item (5) is attached here because these notions are defined over the preferred families.

components.gap: The worked boundary added for this warning contains an incorrect step. Body line 452 says that in C_2 the observation can hold with every hypothesis false 'because m is exogenous', but lines 411-412 identify a,b,c,m with endogenous vertices, and def:p16-finite-scm (finite-causal-models.tex l. 71) reserves 'exogenous' for the disturbances U_i. In C_2, m is an endogenous vertex with no endogenous parent and equation m=U_m (as the annex proof says at l. 379), and the countervaluation also needs U_a and U_b false so that a=m\land U_a and b=U_b\land(m\lor\neg c) are false. Restate the reason in the chapter's terms.
